fields.title: 当天主题（中文短语）
fields.reading: 阅读篇目：英文原文 + 中文翻译 + 一句阅读提示

posts.title: Geology 地质 · 具体比正确重要

reading.why: 这段覆盖今天全部 10 个词。读的时候别查字典——先猜，读完再回头看词表，你会发现它们在句子里有了位置。

speaking.q: Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what the decision was; when you made it; what alternatives you had; and explain why you think it was important.
speaking.ans:
The decision I'd describe is deciding to leave a stable job without having another one lined up. That was about a year ago.

At the time the choice looked different from how it looks now. On paper I had two options: stay, keep the salary and the title, and wait for a better moment to move; or leave and figure out the next thing while looking. The reasonable choice was obviously the first one. Almost everyone I trusted said so, and they weren't being unkind — they were right about the risk.

What made me leave was a realisation that was not really about the job. I noticed that I'd been choosing the second-best version of a career I wasn't sure I wanted. Staying would have been comfortable and it would have made the next decision harder, not easier, because every year the salary gets a bit better and the switching cost gets a bit higher.

Was it a good decision? I don't think I'm the right person to judge yet, honestly. What I can say is that it forced me to find out what I'm actually good at, rather than what I've done before. That's worth something even if the timing turns out to have been bad.
speaking.note: 「我不知道这决定好不好」这种诚实比「这是我最正确的决定」高级得多。注意「choosing the second-best version of a career」是全文最强的一句。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的决定。保留「承认风险、不确定结论」的态度——考官更信这个。

speaking.q: What do you usually do at weekends?
speaking.ans: It depends on how the week went. If I've been staring at a screen for five days, I try to spend Saturday somewhere with no signal — a long walk, or a book in a café where nobody knows me. Sunday is more practical: I plan the week, catch up on the reading I skipped, and try not to panic about Monday.
speaking.note: 「It depends」开头很好，避免变成一个贫乏的清单。「where nobody knows me」这种细节很生动。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的周末节奏。保留「周六恢复 / 周日准备」这个对照结构。

speaking.q: Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books?
speaking.ans: Paper, though not for the reason people usually give. I don't think paper is inherently more romantic — it's that I can't skim a physical book convincingly. On a screen I scroll and convince myself I've read the page. With paper, my eye has to travel across every line, so I actually finish what I start.
speaking.note: 不要重复「纸质书有味道」这种陈词。给一个功能性理由（物理限制导致真读完了）更有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你确实更爱电子书，就说它的理由：搜索、随身、便宜。关键是给出「别人没想到的理由」。

posts.wordtips: 今天这 10 个词里，优先掌握出现频率最高的那三四个；其余的先做到「见到能认出来」，写作时自然会用上。

posts.title: 教育与学习 · 为什么我重新开始学英语

reading.why: 教育类是雅思写作和口语 Part 3 的第一大话题。今天这段覆盖 10 个核心词，读完请用中文说出「死记硬背 vs 批判性思维」这对矛盾。

speaking.ans: I do now, though I didn't when I was younger. At school, English was just another subject I had to pass — I memorised vocabulary lists and forgot them within a week. Things changed when I started reading music criticism in English. I wanted to understand why a reviewer called an album 'deceptively simple', and that curiosity did what ten years of exams couldn't. So now I'd say I learn languages out of appetite rather than obligation.
speaking.note: 结构：现在的答案 → 转折 → 一个具体的触发点。考官最想听「一个具体细节」，不是「英语很重要」。
speaking.swap: 把 reading music criticism 换成你自己真实的触发点：看美剧、和一个外国朋友聊天、读论文、听播客。

speaking.q: Do you think it's important to learn a second language?
speaking.ans: I think it changes what you can access rather than simply adding a skill. My work involves a lot of reading about AI products, and the best material is still published in English first — by the time something is translated, the conversation has moved on. Beyond that, there's a subtler benefit: when you speak a language badly but willingly, you get used to being wrong in public, and that turns out to be useful in almost every other part of life.
speaking.note: 两个层次：实用层（获取信息）+ 心理层（容忍犯错）。第二层是 7 分以上的加分点。
speaking.swap: 把 AI products 换成你的行业；「being wrong in public」这个观察很通用，可以保留。

speaking.q: Describe a subject you found difficult but now find interesting. You should say: what the subject was; when you studied it; why it was difficult; and explain why your attitude changed.
speaking.ans:
I'd like to talk about statistics. I first met it during my master's degree in finance, and I have to admit I struggled badly. The formulas themselves weren't the problem — I could follow the algebra. What defeated me was that I couldn't see what any of it was for. We were asked to compute confidence intervals for abstract datasets, and I remember thinking that this had nothing to do with anything I cared about.

It was difficult for a second reason, which is less flattering. I'd been good at exams my whole life by being good at memorising, and statistics doesn't reward that. You can memorise the formula and still get the interpretation wrong. It exposed a habit I'd been relying on for years.

My attitude changed quite suddenly, when I started working on real data. I was asked to judge whether a difference in survey results between two regions was meaningful or just noise, and I realised I finally had a reason to care. Once the question was concrete, the statistics stopped being abstract machinery and became the only honest way to answer it. Now I find it genuinely elegant — it's a discipline for admitting how little you can actually conclude, which is rarer and more valuable than it sounds.
speaking.note: Part 2 拿高分的关键是「讲一个变化」而不是「描述一个科目」。注意用了两层困难 + 一个转折点 + 一个现在的评价。全程约 2 分钟。
speaking.swap: 如果你不想讲统计，可换成：编程 / 会计 / 数据可视化。把「我喜欢记忆式学习」这个自我观察保留，它让你显得真实。

posts.wordtips: 今天 10 个词里，最值得直接用在作文的是 critical thinking、vocational training、academic performance。rote learning 和 peer pressure 是「负面词」，写议论文时用来描述问题很顺手。

posts.title: 环境 · 干旱地区农业创新

defs: n. 标签,附属物,名称,碎片,结束语,口头禅,陈词滥调,附加语,浑名, 标记
words.ex: Each item in the recycling bin carries a tag showing which materials can be processed.
words.zh: 回收箱里的每件物品都贴有标签，标明哪些材料可以被处理。

words.ex: Historians believe the ancient letters were sealed with wax to protect their contents.
words.zh: 历史学家认为这些古代信件用蜡封口以保护内容。

words.ex: Few crops can survive in such an arid climate, where rainfall is extremely rare.
words.zh: 在如此干旱的气候中，降雨极为稀少，很少有作物能存活。

defs: n.轴(常为虚构之线，如地球轴)
words.ex: The Earth rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours, causing day and night.
words.zh: 地球每二十四小时绕地轴自转一周，从而产生昼夜。

words.ex: The dog began to bark loudly whenever strangers approached the farmhouse gate.
words.zh: 每当陌生人走近农舍大门，那条狗就会大声吠叫。

words.ex: The old wooden barn now serves as a workshop where local artists display their work.
words.zh: 这座旧木谷仓如今成了当地艺术家展示作品的工作室。

defs: n. 边,边缘,(河)边vt. 注满,使满溢vi. 满溢
words.ex: She filled the cup to the brim with hot tea and carefully carried it to the table.
words.zh: 她把杯子斟满热茶，小心地端到桌上。

defs: n. 植物的球茎，球形物; 灯泡
words.ex: Replacing traditional light bulbs with energy-saving ones can greatly reduce electricity consumption.
words.zh: 用节能灯泡替换传统灯泡可以大大降低电力消耗。

defs: 蜂房巢室；细胞；单人牢房
n. 细胞; 单人房间; 基层组织
words.ex: The honeycomb is made up of thousands of hexagonal cells built by worker bees.
words.zh: 蜂巢由工蜂建造的成千上万个六边形巢室组成。

words.ex: Students must cite all sources properly, or their essays may be rejected for plagiarism.
words.zh: 学生必须正确引用所有资料来源，否则论文可能因抄袭而被拒。

reading.en: In many **arid** regions, agricultural innovation has become a vital **axis** of sustainable development, since conventional farming often struggles where rainfall is scarce. One promising approach involves cultivating crops beneath a protective layer of **wax**, which significantly reduces water loss from the soil surface. Researchers also **cite** traditional practices, such as using **bark** mulch, as evidence that local knowledge can complement modern techniques. Meanwhile, engineers have redesigned the **barn** so that its roof **brim** channels rare rainwater into storage tanks, and a single solar **bulb** now lights the interior at night. Each storage **cell** within these tanks preserves every precious drop, while the **tag** of “climate-smart farming” has helped attract international funding. Although critics sometimes **bark** that such projects are too costly, pilot studies suggest they raise yields substantially. Consequently, this integrated model deserves serious consideration wherever drought threatens food security.
reading.zh: 在许多**干旱**地区，农业创新已成为可持续发展的关键**轴心**，因为传统耕作在降雨稀少的地方往往举步维艰。一种前景可观的方法是在一层保护性**蜡**下种植作物，这能显著减少土壤表面的水分流失。研究人员还**引用**诸如使用**树皮**覆盖物等传统做法，作为本地知识能够补充现代技术的证据。与此同时，工程师重新设计了**谷仓**，使其屋顶**边缘**将稀少的雨水引入储水箱，而一盏太阳能**灯泡**如今在夜间照亮内部。这些水箱中的每个储水**单元**都保存着每一滴珍贵的水，而“气候智能型农业”的**称号**也帮助吸引了国际资金。尽管批评者有时会**大声抱怨**此类项目成本过高，但试点研究表明它们能大幅提高产量。因此，在干旱威胁粮食安全的任何地方，这一综合模式都值得认真考虑。
reading.why: 这段把你今天的 10 个词全串起来了。读第一遍别查词——先按上下文猜；读完再看上面的词表，你会发现这些词在句子里各自有了位置。

speaking.q: Do you prefer to spend time with a large group or a few close friends?
speaking.ans: A few, definitely. I'm not shy exactly, but I find large groups exhausting in a way I can't fully explain — I come home feeling like I've been performing rather than talking. With two or three people I can be slower and more honest, and I've noticed that's when I actually remember the conversation afterwards.
speaking.note: 「performing rather than talking」是很精准的对比。用「我记得那次对话」作为证据，比空说「我更放松」有说服力。
speaking.swap: 如果你更爱大群体，就说它的好处：能量、随机性、认识新人。保持「用具体体验作证据」的结构。

speaking.ans:
I'd want to distinguish preserving a tradition from preserving the practice of it, because those often conflict.

There's a strong case for keeping the knowledge. If a craft or a form of music disappears, you lose something you can't reconstruct from a description — the technique lives in people, not in documents. In that sense preservation is genuinely urgent.

The weaker case is the one that gets made most often, which is that a tradition should continue simply because it's old. Age isn't an argument; plenty of old things were bad ideas. And there's a real cost to this framing, because it tends to freeze practices that were always changing, turning something living into a museum piece.

So I'd say: preserve the knowledge, be sceptical of the obligation. The traditions that survive are usually the ones people keep choosing, not the ones they're told to keep.
speaking.note: 「preserve the knowledge vs preserve the obligation」这个拆分是全篇骨架。最后一句「活下来的是人们仍在选择的东西」很有力。
speaking.swap: 这类「应该保留 X 吗」的题，核心动作是「把 X 拆成两种东西」，然后分别判断。

speaking.q: Do you work or are you a student?
speaking.ans: I'm working, though the honest description is that I'm between two things. My background is in finance — I did a master's in that — but for the past year or so I've been working on AI products, which is a fairly big jump. Right now I'm taking some time to prepare for the next step, which involves both studying and job hunting.
speaking.note: 「between two things」比直接说「我在找工作」体面且真实。主动说出转折，反而让后面的话题有抓手。
speaking.swap: 把 finance→AI 换成你自己的转折。核心句式：My background is X, but recently I've been Y.

posts.wordtips: 今天这 10 个词里，tag、wax、arid 最值得先吃透；其余的做到「见到能认出来」，写作时自然会想起来。

posts.title: 教育 · 数字化档案与教育公平

words.ex: Ancient potters shaped clay into bowls and left them to dry in the sun.
words.zh: 古代陶工把黏土捏成碗，然后放在阳光下晾干。

defs: n. 圆锥体,球果vt. 使成锥形
words.ex: The volcano's perfect cone shape attracts thousands of tourists to the island each year.
words.zh: 这座火山完美的锥形每年吸引成千上万的游客来到该岛。

defs: 把...塞进；（为应考）临时死记硬背
vt. 塞满,填满,猛吃vi. 贪吃n. 塞满
v.（超限）填塞，塞满；临时抱佛脚，为考试而学习
words.ex: Many students cram all night before exams instead of reviewing material gradually.
words.zh: 许多学生在考试前通宵死记硬背，而不是循序渐进地复习。

defs: n. 湿气a. 潮湿的vt. 使潮湿,阻尼,抑止vi. 变潮湿,衰减
words.ex: The basement felt cold and damp, so we bought a machine to remove the moisture.
words.zh: 地下室又冷又潮湿，所以我们买了一台机器来除湿。

defs: 散发 (光、热、气等)；发出（声音）
words.ex: Older vehicles emit far more harmful gases than modern electric cars do.
words.zh: 老旧车辆排放的有害气体远远多于现代电动汽车。

defs: n. 史诗; a. 英雄的
n.叙事诗，史诗；a.英雄的；大规模的
words.ex: The film is an epic story of migration, spanning three generations across two continents.
words.zh: 这部电影是一部跨越两大洲三代人的史诗般的迁徙故事。

defs: 均匀的；偶数的；相等的。甚至
a. 平坦的,偶数的,相等的,均匀的,连贯的,均等的,公平的,荹玫?平静的,
words.ex: The paint must be applied in an even layer, or the wall will look patchy.
words.zh: 涂料必须均匀地涂上一层，否则墙面会显得斑驳。

defs: n. 档案; 行列; v. 归档; 提出
words.ex: Please file these documents alphabetically so that they can be found quickly.
words.zh: 请按字母顺序把这些文件归档，以便快速查找。

defs: n. 缺点,裂纹,瑕疵,一阵狂风
words.ex: The main flaw in the study is that it ignores the influence of family background.
words.zh: 这项研究的主要缺陷是忽略了家庭背景的影响。

defs: 掷；快速翻转。随便的；宽泛的
vt. 掷,弹,轻击,空翻vi. 用指轻弹,抽打,蹦跳n. 抛,弹,筋斗
words.ex: The teacher asked students to flip the card over and read the question on the back.
words.zh: 老师让学生把卡片翻过来，读背面的问题。

reading.en: The shift toward digital learning archives has been celebrated as an **epic** advance in educational equity, yet a closer look reveals a troubling **flaw**: uneven access to reliable infrastructure. In many rural schools, students must **cram** into overcrowded rooms where the only computer is a battered laptop, and connectivity is as fragile as **damp** paper. Such conditions hardly **emit** the promise of modern pedagogy. Even worse, teachers rarely have time to **file** each learner's progress systematically, so valuable data simply vanish. To address this, policymakers should **flip** the current funding model and direct resources toward the most underserved districts rather than scattering them in an **even** but ineffective layer. A simple **clay** model of a **cone**, used in a hands-on science lesson, may teach more than a dozen disconnected tablets; meaningful investment, not technological theatre, is what genuine reform requires.
reading.zh: 向数字化学习档案的转变被誉为教育公平的一次**宏大**进步，然而细看之下却暴露出一个令人不安的**缺陷**：可靠基础设施的获取并不均衡。在许多乡村学校，学生不得不**挤**进拥挤的教室，唯一的电脑是一台破旧的笔记本电脑，网络连接像**潮湿**的纸张一样脆弱。这样的条件几乎无法**散发**现代教学法的希望。更糟的是，教师很少有时间系统地**归档**每个学习者的进步，因此宝贵的数据就这样消失了。为解决这一问题，政策制定者应当**翻转**当前的资助模式，把资源投向最缺乏服务的地区，而不是把它们分散成**均匀**却无效的一层。在动手科学课上使用一个简单的**黏土****圆锥**模型，或许比十几台互不相连的平板电脑教得更多；真正有意义的投入，而非技术作秀，才是真正改革所需要的。
reading.why: 这段把你今天的 10 个词全串起来了。读第一遍别查词——先按上下文猜；读完再看上面的词表，你会发现这些词在句子里各自有了位置。

speaking.ans: Two reasons, and they're not equally noble. The practical one is that most of the material I need for work is published in English first — by the time a decent article gets translated, the conversation has moved on. The less practical reason is that I want to be able to read a novel without feeling like I'm doing homework. That's the goal I actually care about.
speaking.note: 「not equally noble」是很好的自我觉察式表达。把功利理由和私人理由并列，比只说一个更真实。
speaking.swap: 把 practical reason 换成你的真实需求（考试、工作、移民、追剧）。

speaking.q: What kind of weather do you like?
speaking.ans: Overcast, which people find strange. Bright sun makes me feel like I should be outside doing something useful; grey weather gives me permission to stay in and read. I spent a winter in a place where it dropped to minus twenty, and oddly that was the most comfortable I've been — the cold was so serious that nobody expected you to be productive.
speaking.note: 反直觉的偏好（喜欢阴天）立刻抓住注意。后面用真实经历做支撑。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的天气偏好 + 一个支撑它的记忆。

speaking.q: Describe a skill you learned that took a long time. You should say: what the skill is; when you learned it; how you learned it; and explain why it took so long.
speaking.ans:
The skill I'd describe is writing clearly — not writing well, which is a different and much rarer thing, but writing in a way that doesn't waste the reader's time. I've been working on it for about four years and I'm still not done.

I started because I had to. My job involved writing analysis that other people had to act on, and I kept getting the same response: 'I'm not sure what you're telling me to do.' That was humbling. I thought I was being thorough. I was being long.

The way I learned was mostly by deleting. I'd write something, cut it in half, and see what survived. Then someone showed me that most of what I was cutting was the part where I explained that I wasn't sure. The uncertainty was real, but burying it in caveats made the whole document useless.

Why it takes so long is that the skill isn't grammatical — it's deciding what matters. You can learn grammar in months. Judging relevance takes years, because you have to be wrong in front of people a lot of times first. I'm better than I was. I still over-explain when I'm nervous.
speaking.note: 「writing clearly 不是 writing well」这个区分很好。最后一句「我紧张时还是会解释太多」收了漂亮的自知之明。
speaking.swap: 换成你真实的技能（开车、做饭、编曲、数据分析）。核心是「为什么它慢」要给一个认知层面的理由，不是「需要多练」。

posts.wordtips: 今天这 10 个词里，clay、cone、cram 最值得先吃透；其余的做到「见到能认出来」，写作时自然会想起来。
